candidates: When writing a function that detects whether a configuration is already fully set up (e.g., to skip redundant postinstall steps), ensure it verifies ALL required components of the intended setup — not just a subset. A partial check (e.g., confirming only that the plugin is imported, without also confirming that `setupFiles` is configured) can cause setup to be skipped even when the configuration is incomplete, leaving users in a broken or partially configured state.

Avoid extracting trivial single-expression predicate helpers whose entire body is a simple equality check or similarly one-liner expression (e.g., `function isFoo(v) { return v === SOME_CONSTANT; }`). Inline the expression at the call site instead; a named wrapper for something that trivial adds indirection without meaningful abstraction or reuse benefit.

Do not duplicate log/message strings across multiple code paths that emit the same message. Extract repeated strings to a named constant and reference it from every call site, so the message only needs to be updated in one place.
